newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian equities end 1996 stronger in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian equities end 1996 stronger in thin trade.

text.p: Nigerian stocks ended the year in an upbeat mood on Tuesday in light but brisk trading.
The all-share index surged to 6992.10 after stagnating at 6982.94 on Monday and last Friday.
Traders said most shares were inactive as most operators were already on vacation, adding only 24 brokers participated in Tuesday's session, a far cry from the usual average of 50.
Gainers included West African Portland Cement company and food company Nestle, both among the best performers this year.
The cement firm rose to 46.40 naira, up 20 kobo and Nestle ended 25 kobo more at 49.25 naira.
Oil shares ended generally higher. Total closed 60 kobo up at 58.00 naira, Texaco added 40 kobo to end at 33.50 naira while African Petroleum was 15 kobo better at 45.00 naira.
Packaging firm Avon Crowncaps slumped five kobo to 2.95 naira and construction company Costain was 1.93, down two kobo.
Aba Textiles dropped one kobo at 3.66 naira, the same as second-tier shares Krabo and Tropical Petroleum, ending at 16 kobo and 34 kobo, respectively.
Traders said the outlook for the market depended on government's economic policy thrust in the 1997 budget.
They said not much business would be done before the budget is released. It is traditionally broadcast by the head of state on New Year day but has come later in recent years.

"Nobody knows when the government will come out with the budget and a lot depends on it," one trader said. "Investors will maintain a wait-and-see-attitude." The 1996 budget was released six weeks late on February 15. ($1=80 naira)
